readings.title: Privilege criteria — initial appointment (LARK-PRIV-2026.1)

paragraphs.text: Privilege criteria — initial appointment

Larkhollow Community Hospital · Medical Staff Office Criteria version LARK-PRIV-2026.1, in force from 2026-01-01. Set by the Clinical Director with the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff. Published and applied by the Medical Staff Office. The office applies these criteria; the office does not write them and does not extend them for an individual applicant.
Every decision record cites the criteria version it was decided under. A file decided under one version is not re-read under another; a new version re-opens the mapping for files not yet decided.

The manual we adopted says what criteria must cover, in Section 9: "At a minimum, privilege criteria should address the required education level, formal training requirements, and current experience." The three columns below are those three.
The twelve privilege groups
Every group requires a Doctor of Medicine or Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine degree from an accredited school, so the education level is not repeated in each row.
Code
Privilege group
Certifications that support it
Minimum training
Current experience
PRIV-FM
Family Medicine — outpatient and inpatient care of patients of any age
American Board of Family Medicine (ABFM), Family Medicine; American Osteopathic Board of Family Physicians (AOBFP), Family Practice
Completion of an accredited family medicine residency, 36 months
Patient care in the specialty within the last 24 months
PRIV-IM
Internal Medicine — outpatient and inpatient care of adults
American Board of Internal Medicine (ABIM), Internal Medicine; American Osteopathic Board of Internal Medicine (AOBIM), Internal Medicine
Completion of an accredited internal medicine residency, 36 months
Patient care in the specialty within the last 24 months
PRIV-HOSP
Hospital Medicine — adult inpatient care, admission and attending

American Board of Internal Medicine (ABIM), Internal Medicine; American Board of Internal Medicine (ABIM), Internal Medicine with Focused Practice in Hospital Medicine; American Board of Family Medicine (ABFM), Family Medicine; American Osteopathic Board of Internal Medicine (AOBIM), Internal Medicine
Completion of an accredited internal medicine residency or an accredited family medicine residency, 36 months
Inpatient care within the last 24 months
PRIV-CARD
Cardiovascular Disease — consultative cardiology, non-invasive testing
American Board of Internal Medicine (ABIM), Cardiovascular Disease; American Osteopathic Board of Internal Medicine (AOBIM), Cardiology
Completion of an accredited cardiovascular disease fellowship, 36 months, in addition to an accredited internal medicine residency
Cardiology practice within the last 24 months
PRIV-EM
Emergency Medicine — emergency department care of patients of any age
American Board of Emergency Medicine (ABEM), Emergency Medicine; American Osteopathic Board of Emergency Medicine (AOBEM), Emergency Medicine
Completion of an accredited emergency medicine residency, 36 months
Emergency department practice within the last 24 months
PRIV-GS
General Surgery — elective and emergency general surgical procedures
American Board of Surgery (ABS), Surgery; American Osteopathic Board of Surgery (AOBS), General Surgery
Completion of an accredited general surgery residency, 60 months
Operative practice within the last 24 months
PRIV-OBG
Obstetrics and Gynecology — obstetric and gynaecological care and surgery
American Board of Obstetrics and Gynecology (ABOG), Obstetrics and Gynecology; American Osteopathic Board of Obstetrics and Gynecology (AOBOG)
Completion of an accredited obstetrics and gynecology residency, 48 months
Obstetric or gynaecological practice within the last 24 months
PRIV-PED
Pediatrics — outpatient and inpatient care of patients under 18
American Board of Pediatrics (ABP), Pediatrics; American Osteopathic Board of Pediatrics (AOBP), Pediatrics
Completion of an accredited pediatrics residency, 36 months
Patient care in the specialty within the last 24 months
PRIV-ANES
Anesthesiology — general and regional anaesthesia, peri-operative care
American Board of Anesthesiology (ABA), Anesthesiology; American Osteopathic Board of Anesthesiology (AOBA)
Completion of an accredited anesthesiology residency, 48 months
Anaesthetic practice within the last 24 months
PRIV-RAD
Diagnostic Radiology — interpretation of diagnostic imaging
American Board of Radiology (ABR), Diagnostic Radiology; American Osteopathic Board of Radiology (AOBR), Diagnostic Radiology
Completion of an accredited diagnostic radiology residency, 48 months
Interpretive practice within the last 24 months
PRIV-PSY
Psychiatry — inpatient and outpatient psychiatric care of adults
American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology (ABPN), Psychiatry; American Osteopathic Board of Neurology and Psychiatry (AOBNP), Psychiatry
Completion of an accredited psychiatry residency, 48 months
Psychiatric practice within the last 24 months
PRIV-ORTHO
Orthopaedic Surgery — elective and trauma orthopaedic procedures
American Board of Orthopaedic Surgery (ABOS), Orthopaedic Surgery; American Osteopathic Board of Orthopedic Surgery (AOBOS), Orthopedic Surgery
Completion of an accredited orthopaedic surgery residency, 60 months
Operative practice within the last 24 months
The boards named above are real certifying bodies. Nothing in these materials is a statement about any practitioner they have actually certified.
How the office applies the table

A requested group is supported when the applicant holds a verified certification from one of the boards named in that group's row, in the specialty named, with certification_status Active on the decision date, and the verified training meets the minimum training requirement.
A requested group is unsupported when neither condition holds. The finding names that group. Other requested groups are unaffected.

An inactive or expired certification does not support a privilege group. It is still verified and still recorded — what the applicant is certified in and what the applicant was once certified in are different facts — but it supports nothing.

Board eligible is accepted in place of an active certification for PRIV-FM, PRIV-IM, PRIV-HOSP and PRIV-PED only, and only when the issuing board confirms in writing that the applicant is a candidate in good standing and states the date the eligibility ends, and that date is in the future on the decision date. Board eligible is not accepted for PRIV-CARD, PRIV-EM, PRIV-GS, PRIV-OBG, PRIV-ANES, PRIV-RAD, PRIV-PSY or PRIV-ORTHO.

PRIV-CARD requires both: the cardiovascular disease fellowship and the internal medicine residency that precedes it. A cardiology certification without the residency, or the residency without the fellowship, does not support it.

When nothing the applicant holds supports any requested group, this is a threshold eligibility question. The office raises it to the Clinical Director, who decides whether the application is discontinued. The office does not discontinue an application. The office raises it on what has been verified at the export date: while nothing yet verified supports any requested group, the question stands with the Clinical Director, and it is withdrawn without a disposition when a later verification supports the request.

The current-experience column is not the office's to apply. Current competency is determined by clinical leadership, not the office (the manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 8), and it is one of the elements this procedure does not handle. Whether a group is supported is decided by rules 1 to 6 alone; the current-experience requirement travels with the packet for the committee and never makes a group unsupported.
Whether a supported request should be granted is not settled here. That is the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff's recommendation and the Governing Body's decision.

Larkhollow Community Hospital · Medical Staff Office Criteria version LARK-PRIV-2026.1, in force from 2026-01-01. Set by the Clinical Director with the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff. Published and applied by the Medical Staff Office. The office applies these criteria; the office does not write them and does not extend them for an individual applicant.
Every decision record cites the criteria version it was decided under. A file decided under one version is not re-read under another; a new version re-opens the mapping for files not yet decided.
The manual we adopted says what criteria must cover, in Section 9: "At a minimum, privilege criteria should address the required education level, formal training requirements, and current experience." The three columns below are those three.
The twelve privilege groups
Every group requires a Doctor of Medicine or Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine degree from an accredited school, so the education level is not repeated in each row.

The boards named above are real certifying bodies. Nothing in these materials is a statement about any practitioner they have actually certified.
How the office applies the table
A requested group is supported when the applicant holds a verified certification from one of the boards named in that group's row, in the specialty named, with certification_status Active on the decision date, and the verified training meets the minimum training requirement.
A requested group is unsupported when neither condition holds. The finding names that group. Other requested groups are unaffected.
An inactive or expired certification does not support a privilege group. It is still verified and still recorded — what the applicant is certified in and what the applicant was once certified in are different facts — but it supports nothing.
Board eligible is accepted in place of an active certification for PRIV-FM, PRIV-IM, PRIV-HOSP and PRIV-PED only, and only when the issuing board confirms in writing that the applicant is a candidate in good standing and states the date the eligibility ends, and that date is in the future on the decision date. Board eligible is not accepted for PRIV-CARD, PRIV-EM, PRIV-GS, PRIV-OBG, PRIV-ANES, PRIV-RAD, PRIV-PSY or PRIV-ORTHO.
PRIV-CARD requires both: the cardiovascular disease fellowship and the internal medicine residency that precedes it. A cardiology certification without the residency, or the residency without the fellowship, does not support it.
When nothing the applicant holds supports any requested group, this is a threshold eligibility question. The office raises it to the Clinical Director, who decides whether the application is discontinued. The office does not discontinue an application. The office raises it on what has been verified at the export date: while nothing yet verified supports any requested group, the question stands with the Clinical Director, and it is withdrawn without a disposition when a later verification supports the request.
The current-experience column is not the office's to apply. Current competency is determined by clinical leadership, not the office (the manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 8), and it is one of the elements this procedure does not handle. Whether a group is supported is decided by rules 1 to 6 alone; the current-experience requirement travels with the packet for the committee and never makes a group unsupported.
Whether a supported request should be granted is not settled here. That is the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff's recommendation and the Governing Body's decision.

readings.title: How this office exports its credentialing records (office note, 2026-03-16)

paragraphs.text: How this office exports its credentialing records
Larkhollow Community Hospital · Medical Staff Office A note from the Medical Services Professional to whoever automates the initial-appointment file. Written 2026-03-16, alongside the first export.

I run the export from the credentialing database every few weeks and drop it in the shared folder, one sub-folder per export. Here is what you get, what the columns mean, and the three or four things that catch people out.
The export date is the clock

Every batch folder has a README.md that says the export date and the window it covers. That date is the clock for everything in the folder: nothing in a batch happened after its export date. Work the batch as if today were the export date. Do not use the real date you run your tool, and do not carry today's date into an arithmetic that a batch is supposed to settle.

The three exports are 2026-03-16, 2026-04-20 and 2026-05-18. The first one covers everything on file up to and including 2026-03-15, however far back it goes — one application here was first received in 2024. The second and third cover only what changed since the previous one.

The caseload at an export date is every application file the office has received up to that date, however that file ended. A withdrawn or discontinued file stays in the caseload with its final status; a later batch never removes a file, it only adds to what is known about it.
A batch is closed. It never changes.

I never go back and edit an export. If an applicant corrects something, a new revision of the application appears in a later batch and the old one stays exactly where it was. If a board sends a corrected reply, the corrected reply is a new row and the old row stays. If a committee decides something twice, there are two decision records.
So: do not diff a later batch against an earlier one looking for edits. There are none. What a later batch contains is new rows, new documents and new observations.
The files
Thirteen comma-separated exports, and three folders of documents.
File
One row is
applications.csv
an application revision I received in the window
application-disclosures.csv
one professional practice question and the applicant's answer
declared-history.csv
one history entry the applicant declared
declared-credentials.csv
one licence or certification as the applicant described it
privilege-requests.csv
one privilege group requested
licence-lookup-wa.csv
one Washington credential record from the state board's lookup
licence-lookup-other-states.csv
one out-of-state credential record
certification-replies.csv
one certifying board's reply
verification-replies.csv
one reply about education and training, or about an affiliation or employer
verification-attempts.csv
one request I sent
peer-referees.csv
one referee named on an application, or supplied later
peer-reference-replies.csv
one completed reference form that came back
correspondence.csv
one letter, memo or decision record, with the path to the document
Folder
What is in it
letters/
applicants' explanation letters, withdrawals, referee substitutions, and my own written requests for missing items
dispositions/
the Clinical Director's recorded dispositions
decisions/
Credentials Committee and Executive Committee minutes extracts, and Governing Body approval records
correspondence.csv is an index. It tells you the documents exist and where they are. It does not tell you what they say — you have to open them.
A file with only a header row means the export ran and there was nothing in that window. That is not the same as a missing file, and it is not an error.
Dates, blanks and columns

Dates are YYYY-MM-DD. Always. A date range is inclusive at both ends: an entry from_date 2022-01-01, to_date 2022-12-31 covers the 1st of January and the 31st of December. An expiry date is the last day the credential is valid.

An empty cell means I hold no value for that field. It does not mean zero, it does not mean "no", and it does not mean the answer is unknown-but-probably-fine. Two blanks carry a specific meaning and you should learn them:
a blank to_date in declared-history.csv means the entry is current, running to the export date — not that the end date is missing;
a blank expiry_date in certification-replies.csv means the certificate does not expire — some older certificates are time-unlimited.
No money appears anywhere. We do not record fees, salaries or contract values in the credentialing file.
Files are UTF-8 with Unix line endings. Values are quoted only when they contain a comma.
The three joins that matter

Everything on the applicant side joins on application_id, and on revision where the fact belongs to a revision. Entries, credentials, privilege requests and disclosures all restate on each revision, so always filter to the revision you are working.

The Washington board export carries no practitioner identifier. It never has. I join it to an application on lastname, firstname, middlename and birthyear. I have checked that no two rows in any one export share those four values, so the join gives you at most one row. An applicant with no row in that file holds no Washington credential. The absence is the answer, not a data problem.

A referee with no row in peer-reference-replies.csv has not replied. Silence produces no record. You can see it only by looking at the requests in verification-attempts.csv and finding no reply against them.
The Washington export's own columns

I pass that file through as the board publishes it and add one column. The board's twelve are credentialnumber, credentialtype, status, firstissuedate, lastissuedate, expirationdate, ceduedate, actiontaken, birthyear, firstname, middlename, lastname. Mine is lookup_date — the day I ran the lookup. It is my own act, not a source's reply, so the usability window is not applied to it.
Two of the board's columns are easy to misread:
ceduedate is a continuing-education due date. We do not use it. Continuing education is handled outside this procedure and it has nothing to do with whether a licence is valid.

actiontaken says the board has acted. It does not say what the action was. For that you need the board's written reply, which arrives as a document, not in this file. A Yes here is a reason to go and read; it is not a conclusion.

The first export carries the board's whole file for our county — 435 rows — so you can see what an ordinary population looks like. The second and third carry only a re-lookup of the practitioners whose files are open, because that is all I re-run.
How often anything is actually wrong
I want to say this plainly, because a small sample of credentialing files can leave the wrong impression.

In the board's population, action against a credential is rare. In the 435-row export you have: 431 rows say No, 3 say Yes, and 1 says Pending. That is 0.69% Yes and 0.23% Pending, and it is the shape of the real thing — the overwhelming majority of licensed practitioners have a clean board record, and any tool that expects otherwise will be wrong almost every time it fires.

The applicants in these batches are a different matter, and deliberately so. This is a teaching set. I have put every situation the procedure has a rule for into these three exports on purpose, so the run has something to exercise: a restricted licence, an unexplained gap, a school that closed, a referee who never answers, a certificate that lapsed, a decision against the wrong revision. A real nine weeks of intake would be far quieter than this. Do not read the applicant set as a base rate. Read it as a checklist that happens to be shaped like a caseload.
The clean files are genuinely clean. If your tool raises something on one of them, it is your tool.
What I do not export

My own queue, my own statuses and my own conclusions. This export is the evidence, not my reading of it. What is complete, what is outstanding, what is presentable and what is owed to whom is the work — it is not in the folder, and it should not be.

Referee addresses. The export carries no address column for peer referees. The working-address half of completeness condition 7 is checked by my office outside the export, so a run assesses condition 7 on the named referees alone and records the address check as not assessable from the export — neither met nor failed.

readings.title: Application for initial appointment and clinical privileges — blank form (LARK-APP-2026.1)

paragraphs.text: Application for initial appointment and clinical privileges — blank form

Larkhollow Community Hospital · Medical Staff Office Form version LARK-APP-2026.1. This is the blank form. A completed form becomes revision 1 of an application; a correction becomes revision 2, and so on. A revision never replaces the one before it in the file.
Complete every section. An incomplete application is returned with a written list of what is missing, and the reply is due within 30 calendar days of the date on that letter.
Section A — Identity and contact
Field
What to enter
Last name, First name, Middle name
As shown on your licence. Leave middle name blank only if you have none
Birth year
Four digits
Degree
MD or DO
National Provider Identifier
Ten digits, if you hold one. This is an identifier for billing and is not a licence. Entering it does not declare a licence
Practice state
The two-letter state in which you will see patients under this appointment
Position sought
The role this appointment is for
Clinical discipline

The discipline you practise, chosen from: Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, Hospital Medicine, Cardiovascular Disease, Emergency Medicine, General Surgery, Obstetrics and Gynecology, Pediatrics, Anesthesiology, Diagnostic Radiology, Psychiatry, Orthopaedic Surgery. Your peer referees must practise the discipline you name here
Section B — Authorization and release

I authorize Larkhollow Community Hospital to request and receive information about me from any school, training programme, licensing board, certifying board, employer, affiliated institution and professional reference named in this application, and I authorize each of them to release it. I release each of them from liability for doing so.
Signature and date. Until this is signed and dated, the office sends no verification request of any kind, and the application cannot advance.
Section C — Privileges requested
List every privilege group you request, by the code and name published in the current privilege criteria. Name the criteria version you are requesting under. At least one group is required.
Section D — Education and post-graduate training
One row per entry. Medical school first, then every internship, residency, fellowship or other organized professional training, in date order.
Field
What to enter
Entry type
medical-school, residency, fellowship, or other
Organization, Location
The school or sponsoring institution, and its town and state
Role
Degree sought, or the programme and position
From date, To date
YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive
Verification contact name and email
Whom the office should write to
Section E — Employment, affiliations, teaching and military service
One row per entry, in date order, running continuously from the day after you finished professional school to today.
Field
What to enter
Entry type
employment, affiliation, teaching, military, or other
Organization, Location
The employer or institution, and its town and state
Role
Your position
From date, To date
YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. Leave To date blank only if the entry is current
Hours per week
Whole hours. A part-time entry is still an entry
Verification contact name and email
Whom the office should write to
Notes
Anything the dates alone do not explain
Overlapping entries are expected — a part-time clinic post alongside a hospital appointment is two entries, not an error. Enter both.
Section F — Explanation of periods not covered

For every period of 30 days or more since you finished professional school that no entry in Section D or E covers, attach a written explanation. One explanation per period. Begin the explanation with the line Period explained: <from date> to <to date>, and make sure that period covers the whole of the period you are explaining — the office matches your explanation to the period by those two dates and by nothing else.
The office records your explanation. The office does not judge it. Whether an explanation is satisfactory is the Clinical Director's decision.
An application with a period of 30 days or more and no written explanation for it is returned as incomplete.
Section G — Licences and certifications
One row per credential, including every licence and certification you have ever held, active or inactive, in any state and from any board.
Field
What to enter
Class
licence or certification
Issuer
The state board or the certifying board
Jurisdiction or board
Two-letter state for a licence; the board's short code for a certification
Number
The credential number
Status
Your own description: Active, Inactive, Expired, Board certified, Board eligible
Issue date, Expiry date
YYYY-MM-DD
What you enter here is your declaration. The office verifies each entry with the issuing board, and the board's answer is what goes in the file.
Section H — Peer references
Name at least two peer referees. For each: name, credential, organization, specialty, working address, and how you have worked together.

A referee must have worked directly with you within the past two years, must practise in the same clinical discipline, and must not be a relative, spouse or partner. The office writes to each referee directly; a reference you carry to us yourself cannot be used.
Section I — Professional practice questions
Answer every question Yes or No. Every Yes requires a written explanation in the comment box beside it. Leaving a question unanswered makes the application incomplete.
Code
Question
PPQ-1

Has any licence or registration you hold or have held ever been denied, suspended, revoked, restricted, placed on probation, made subject to a monitoring agreement, surrendered, or subjected to any other action by a licensing board?
PPQ-2
Have your clinical privileges at any institution ever been denied, reduced, restricted, suspended, revoked, not renewed, or made subject to conditions?
PPQ-3
Have you ever resigned from, or withdrawn an application to, a medical staff or training programme while an investigation was pending or in exchange for not conducting an investigation?
PPQ-4
Has any board certification you hold or have held ever been revoked, suspended, or not renewed for cause?
PPQ-5
Have you ever been the subject of a professional review action reportable to a national data bank?
PPQ-6
Have you ever been excluded, debarred or suspended from participation in a federal or state health care programme?
PPQ-7
Have you ever been convicted of, or pleaded guilty or no contest to, a criminal offence other than a minor traffic violation?
PPQ-8
Is there any physical or mental condition, or any use of a substance, that currently impairs your ability to perform the privileges you are requesting, with or without accommodation?

A Yes to any of these is a high-risk finding. It is not by itself a bar to appointment. It is routed to the Clinical Director and presented to the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff and to the Governing Body with the evidence.
If a verification the office receives shows that a Yes was owed and a No was given, the office will contact you to confirm the answer before the file goes any further.
Section J — Attestation

I attest that everything in this application is complete, current and correct. I understand that the burden of supplying verifiable information is mine, and that a discrepancy between what I have declared and what a source reports will be put back to me in writing.
Signature and date.
What the office does with a completed form

The office records receipt, screens the nine completeness conditions in the procedure, and either takes the file up or writes to you with the missing items. It then writes to the schools, programmes, boards, employers, affiliations and referees named above. It does not use anything you hand over yourself in place of their replies.

One row per entry, in date order, running continuously from the day after you finished professional school to today.

Overlapping entries are expected — a part-time clinic post alongside a hospital appointment is two entries, not an error. Enter both.
Section F — Explanation of periods not covered
For every period of 30 days or more since you finished professional school that no entry in Section D or E covers, attach a written explanation. One explanation per period. Begin the explanation with the line Period explained: <from date> to <to date>, and make sure that period covers the whole of the period you are explaining — the office matches your explanation to the period by those two dates and by nothing else.
The office records your explanation. The office does not judge it. Whether an explanation is satisfactory is the Clinical Director's decision.
An application with a period of 30 days or more and no written explanation for it is returned as incomplete.
Section G — Licences and certifications
One row per credential, including every licence and certification you have ever held, active or inactive, in any state and from any board.

Your own description: Active, Inactive, Expired, Board certified, Board eligible
Issue date, Expiry date
YYYY-MM-DD
What you enter here is your declaration. The office verifies each entry with the issuing board, and the board's answer is what goes in the file.
Section H — Peer references
Name at least two peer referees. For each: name, credential, organization, specialty, working address, and how you have worked together.
A referee must have worked directly with you within the past two years, must practise in the same clinical discipline, and must not be a relative, spouse or partner. The office writes to each referee directly; a reference you carry to us yourself cannot be used.
Section I — Professional practice questions
Answer every question Yes or No. Every Yes requires a written explanation in the comment box beside it. Leaving a question unanswered makes the application incomplete.
Code
Question
PPQ-1
Has any licence or registration you hold or have held ever been denied, suspended, revoked, restricted, placed on probation, made subject to a monitoring agreement, surrendered, or subjected to any other action by a licensing board?
PPQ-2
Have your clinical privileges at any institution ever been denied, reduced, restricted, suspended, revoked, not renewed, or made subject to conditions?
PPQ-3
Have you ever resigned from, or withdrawn an application to, a medical staff or training programme while an investigation was pending or in exchange for not conducting an investigation?
PPQ-4
Has any board certification you hold or have held ever been revoked, suspended, or not renewed for cause?
PPQ-5
Have you ever been the subject of a professional review action reportable to a national data bank?
PPQ-6
Have you ever been excluded, debarred or suspended from participation in a federal or state health care programme?
PPQ-7
Have you ever been convicted of, or pleaded guilty or no contest to, a criminal offence other than a minor traffic violation?
PPQ-8
Is there any physical or mental condition, or any use of a substance, that currently impairs your ability to perform the privileges you are requesting, with or without accommodation?
A Yes to any of these is a high-risk finding. It is not by itself a bar to appointment. It is routed to the Clinical Director and presented to the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff and to the Governing Body with the evidence.
If a verification the office receives shows that a Yes was owed and a No was given, the office will contact you to confirm the answer before the file goes any further.
Section J — Attestation
I attest that everything in this application is complete, current and correct. I understand that the burden of supplying verifiable information is mine, and that a discrepancy between what I have declared and what a source reports will be put back to me in writing.
Signature and date.
What the office does with a completed form
The office records receipt, screens the nine completeness conditions in the procedure, and either takes the file up or writes to you with the missing items. It then writes to the schools, programmes, boards, employers, affiliations and referees named above. It does not use anything you hand over yourself in place of their replies.

paragraphs.text: Professional peer reference — blank request and return form
Larkhollow Community Hospital · Medical Staff Office Form version LARK-REF-2026.1.
The office sends this form directly to the referee the applicant named, and the referee returns it directly to the office. A form that reaches us through the applicant cannot be used.
Part 1 — completed by the Medical Staff Office before sending
Field
Content
Referee identifier
The office's identifier for this referee on this file
Applicant
Name and degree
Privileges requested
The privilege groups on the application
Request date
The date this request was sent
Request number
1, 2 or 3 — each reminder is a fresh numbered request

We write up to three times, 21 calendar days apart. If no reply has reached us by the 64th day after the first request, we tell the applicant and ask for an additional referee. The original request stays open. We do not close it as satisfied and we do not count it.
Part 2 — completed by the referee
Field
What to enter
Are you a relative, spouse or partner of the applicant?
Tick Yes or No. This box is never left blank
Relationship
How you worked with the applicant, in your own words
Your specialty

The clinical discipline you practise, chosen from the same list the applicant chose from: Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, Hospital Medicine, Cardiovascular Disease, Emergency Medicine, General Surgery, Obstetrics and Gynecology, Pediatrics, Anesthesiology, Diagnostic Radiology, Psychiatry, Orthopaedic Surgery — or your own discipline if it is not on that list
Dates you worked directly together
First and last date. Leave the last date blank only if you still work together
Recommendation
Recommend without reservation, Recommend, Recommend with reservations, or Do not recommend
Comments
Character, clinical experience, competency, and anything else you want on the record
Signature and signature date
The date you sign. This is the date we measure currency from — not the date we receive the form
Who may give a peer reference
Three conditions, each independent, all three required:
you have worked directly with the applicant within the two years ending on the day you sign this form;
you practise in the same clinical discipline as the applicant;
you are not a relative, spouse or partner of the applicant.

If any one of the three does not hold, say so on the form and return it anyway. We will record your reply, and we will not count it towards the two references the appointment needs. That is not a judgment about you or about the applicant; it is the rule we apply to every file the same way.
Currency

A reference is current if the signature date is within two years of the date the file is presented to the Governing Body. A reference signed a long time before the file is presented stops being current, and we ask again.
Part 3 — completed by the Medical Staff Office on return
Field
Content
Received date
The date the completed form reached the office
How it arrived
Secure portal, letter, fax or email, direct from the referee

Nothing in Part 2 is edited, summarized or corrected by the office. What the referee wrote is what goes in the file, including a relationship or a specialty that differs from what the applicant told us.

Larkhollow Community Hospital · Medical Staff Office Roster version LARK-AUTH-2026.1, effective 2026-01-01. Maintained by the Medical Staff Office from the Governing Body's appointment records.

Every decision record is validated against this roster. A record that names a signatory and a role is checked here: did that person hold that role on the decision date, and may the body they signed for record that outcome. A record's own claim of authority is not evidence of it.
All names below are fictional.
Who may record what

any approval

recommended, not recommended, deferred-pending-information

readings.content:
# Batch 1 export — Larkhollow Community Hospital, Medical Staff Office

**Export date: 2026-03-16**
**Window covered: everything on file up to and including 2026-03-15**

This folder is a closed export. Nothing in it happened after 2026-03-16, and nothing in it will be
edited. Work it as if today were the export date.

This is the first export. It carries everything on file up to and including 2026-03-15, however far back it goes — one application here was first received in 2024. The state board lookup in this folder is the board's whole file for our county, so you can see what an ordinary population looks like.

## What is here

| File | Rows |
|---|---|
| `applications.csv` | 41 |
| `application-disclosures.csv` | 328 |
| `declared-history.csv` | 155 |
| `declared-credentials.csv` | 86 |
| `privilege-requests.csv` | 46 |

| `verification-attempts.csv` | 236 |
| `peer-referees.csv` | 79 |
| `peer-reference-replies.csv` | 57 |
| `correspondence.csv` | 15 |

| Folder | Documents |
|---|---|
| `letters/` | 9 |
| `dispositions/` | 0 |
| `decisions/` | 6 |

A file with only a header row means the export ran and this window produced nothing of that kind.
That is not a missing file.

readings.content:
# Batch 3 export — Larkhollow Community Hospital, Medical Staff Office

**Export date: 2026-05-18**
**Window covered: 2026-04-20 to 2026-05-17**

This folder is a closed export. Nothing in it happened after 2026-05-18, and nothing in it will be
edited. Work it as if today were the export date.

This export carries what changed between 2026-04-20 and 2026-05-17. The state board lookup is again a re-run against the practitioners with an open file.

## What is here

| File | Rows |
|---|---|
| `applications.csv` | 1 |
| `application-disclosures.csv` | 8 |
| `declared-history.csv` | 5 |
| `declared-credentials.csv` | 3 |
| `privilege-requests.csv` | 1 |

| `peer-referees.csv` | 4 |
| `peer-reference-replies.csv` | 4 |
| `correspondence.csv` | 26 |

| Folder | Documents |
|---|---|
| `letters/` | 4 |
| `dispositions/` | 1 |
| `decisions/` | 21 |

A file with only a header row means the export ran and this window produced nothing of that kind.
That is not a missing file.

The field dictionary, the join rules, the meaning of every blank and the rarity of an adverse
board finding are in `../../office/export-notes.md`. The office's procedure is in
`../../office/procedure-extract.md`. Read both before working this folder.

— Renata Kowalczyk, CPMSM, Medical Services Professional

readings.title: 2026-03-06_missing-licence_APP-2026-031.md
readings.content:
# A Washington licence is required by the bylaws

**Date:** 2026-03-06  
**To:** Dr. Kenji Matsuda, MD  
**Application:** APP-2026-031  
**Applicant:** Dr. Kenji Matsuda, MD  

Thank you for your note of 2026-02-20. A National Provider Identifier is an identifier for billing; it is not a licence and it says nothing about whether anybody is licensed. Your Oregon licence is current and we have verified it, and we will verify every other licence you hold, but Larkhollow's bylaws require one current, active, full and unrestricted licence issued by the State of Washington, which is our practice state. The standard we work to is more generous than ours on this point — it accepts a licence from any state — and we have quoted it beside our own rule in the procedure so you can see the difference. Please tell us as soon as the Washington board issues.

Renata Kowalczyk, CPMSM
Medical Services Professional
Larkhollow Community Hospital, Larkhollow, Washington

The American Board of Surgery reports your surgery certification as inactive, initially issued 2001-07-15 and expired 2019-12-31. Your application declares it as current.
